n: In contrast to the seductress lurking in the dark (chapter 7), Wisdom calls out openly. Wisdom here is personified as a woman who speaks for herself.
She stands on high ground and at the crossroads, where everyone can hear her.

f.g: Where the roads meet—the crossroads.

n: She calls at the city gates and doorways, the busiest public places in an ancient town.

f.g: The gate area was the town’s marketplace and court.

n: Her message is for everyone—all humanity, not just a select few.

f.g: All people, all humankind.

n: She especially invites the naive and the foolish to gain sense. No one is beyond her invitation.
What she offers is noble and right.

f.g: Noble, princely things.

n: Wisdom speaks only truth; wickedness is detestable to her.
Nothing she says is twisted or crooked.

f.g: froward = crooked, perverse.

n: Her words are clear to anyone with discernment and right to those who have found knowledge.

f.g: plain = straightforward, clear.

n: Choose her teaching over silver and knowledge over the best gold.
Wisdom is worth more than precious gems; nothing you could want compares to her.

f.g: Possibly red coral or pearls—something very costly.

n: Wisdom lives with prudence and knows how to plan well. In KJV English, “witty inventions” meant clever, discerning plans—not jokes.

f.g: witty = wise, skillful; “inventions” = plans or discretion. Shrewd, thoughtful planning.
prudence = shrewd good sense.

n: Reverence for the Lord includes hating evil. Wisdom names what she hates: pride, arrogance, evil conduct, and perverse speech.

f.w: The fear of the LORD is to hate evil

n: Good counsel, sound judgment, insight, and strength belong to Wisdom.
Rulers govern well and make just laws through wisdom. Solomon himself had asked God for wisdom to rule.
All leaders—princes, nobles, and judges—need wisdom to lead justly.

f.w: all the judges of the earth

n: Wisdom loves those who love her, and those who seek her earnestly will find her.

f.w: those that seek me early shall find me
f.g: early = earnestly, diligently.

n: Wisdom offers lasting riches and honor—wealth joined with righteousness.

f.g: Lasting, enduring wealth.

n: What wisdom produces is better than the finest gold and silver.

f.g: revenue = yield, income, return.

n: Wisdom walks in the path of righteousness and justice.

f.g: judgment = justice.

n: She endows those who love her with real wealth and fills their storehouses.

f.g: substance = real wealth, what truly exists and lasts.

n: The poem’s high point begins: Wisdom was with the Lord before creation. Many Christians have seen here a foreshadowing of Christ, the Word who was with God in the beginning.

f.g: Hebrew qanani—“acquired,” “possessed,” or “brought forth” me; translators differ.

f.w: in the beginning of his way

n: Wisdom was established from eternity, before the earth existed. Latter-day Saints may recall that intelligence and truth are eternal.

f.w: I was set up from everlasting

n: Before oceans and springs existed, Wisdom was already there.

f.g: The deep waters of the primeval ocean.

n: Before mountains were set in place and hills were formed, Wisdom was brought forth.
Before God had made the land, fields, or even the first specks of soil.

f.w: the highest part of the dust
f.g: Perhaps “the first of the dust”—the earth’s first particles.

n: When God laid out the heavens and drew a circle on the face of the deep—marking the horizon—Wisdom was present.

f.g: compass = circle, boundary—like the horizon drawn over the sea.

n: When God set the clouds in place above and made the deep springs strong.
When God set limits for the sea and laid the earth’s foundations. Creation is pictured as an orderly act of a wise Builder.

f.w: that the waters should not pass his commandment

n: Wisdom was beside God like a master craftsman or a beloved child, delighting before him every day.

f.w: as one brought up with him
f.g: Hebrew ʾamon—either “master workman” or “little child/darling”; scholars debate which.

n: Wisdom rejoiced in the inhabited world and especially delighted in humanity. Creation was made with joy, and people were the crown of it.

f.w: my delights were with the sons of men

n: Wisdom’s appeal: since she was there at creation and knows how the world works, listen to her. Those who follow her ways are blessed.

f.w: blessed are they that keep my ways

n: A simple command: listen to instruction, become wise, and don’t reject it.
The blessed person is like an eager visitor who waits at Wisdom’s door every day, hoping to be let in.
To find Wisdom is to find life and the Lord’s favor. Christians hear an echo of Christ, who said he is the life.
Rejecting Wisdom harms the rejecter. Those who hate her are, in effect, choosing death.

f.w: all they that hate me love death

f.g: Or “misses me”—the Hebrew word for sin means to miss the mark.
